title: Core Professional Skills for Regulatory Staff
summary: An eight-module practical programme building the core writing, analysis, meeting, challenge, presentation and data skills that regulatory staff need every day.
intro: This training programme equips new and developing regulatory staff with the practical professional skills the job demands: clear writing, sound analysis, effective firm meetings, confident challenge and well-organised casework.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip regulatory staff with the everyday professional skills that turn technical knowledge into effective supervisory work. Participants leave able to write clearly, analyse evidence, run and record firm meetings, challenge management constructively, present to committees and manage their caseload and data with discipline.
sections.What It Covers: Regulatory writing, analysis and use of evidence, planning and running firm meetings, challenging management, presenting to committees and panels, time and case management, and working with data and spreadsheets.
Intended Audience: New joiners and developing staff in supervisory, authorisation, policy and enforcement roles
Staff recently promoted into case-handling roles who want to strengthen core skills
Line managers seeking a common standard of professional practice for their teams
Learning Objectives: Write clear, concise and evidence-based regulatory documents for firms and internal audiences
Analyse information critically and distinguish evidence from assertion
Plan, run and record effective meetings with firms
Challenge management confidently, constructively and professionally
Present findings and recommendations persuasively to committees and decision-makers
Manage time, caseload and data with discipline and an auditable record
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a four-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Each module is highly practical, using exercises, role-play and peer feedback, and modules can be selected or tailored to the authority's templates and processes.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: No prior experience is required. The programme is suitable for staff in their first years at the authority as well as those wishing to refresh core skills.
Core Reading: IMF (2010), The Making of Good Supervision: Learning to Say "No" (Staff Position Note SPN/10/08)
IMF (2023), Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181)
FSB (2014), Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture: A Framework for Assessing Risk Culture

modules.title: Writing for Regulatory Purposes
modules.summary: The principles of clear regulatory writing, from structuring an argument to choosing the right tone for letters, file notes and internal papers.
objectives: Structure documents so the key message comes first
Write in plain, precise and defensible language
Adapt style and tone for firms, colleagues and decision-makers
syllabus: Top-down structure: conclusion first, then supporting evidence
Plain language, precision and avoiding ambiguity
Letters to firms, file notes, emails and briefing notes
Exercise: rewriting a weak supervisory letter

modules.title: Analysis, Evidence and Critical Thinking
modules.summary: How to analyse information from firms, test it against other sources and reach conclusions that are supported by evidence rather than assertion.
objectives: Distinguish facts, evidence, opinion and assertion
Test information for reliability, consistency and completeness
Draw proportionate conclusions and record the reasoning behind them
syllabus: Sources of evidence: documents, data, interviews and observation
Corroboration, triangulation and spotting inconsistencies
Common reasoning errors and cognitive bias
Recording analysis so another reviewer can follow it

modules.title: Planning and Running Firm Meetings
modules.summary: How to prepare for, conduct and follow up meetings with firms so that each meeting has a clear purpose and produces usable evidence.
objectives: Set objectives and an agenda for a firm meeting
Use questioning and listening techniques to obtain useful information
Record outcomes accurately and agree follow-up actions
syllabus: Preparation: objectives, information request and roles
Opening, questioning, listening and controlling the meeting
Taking notes and producing an accurate meeting record
Follow-up letters, actions and deadlines

modules.title: Challenging Management with Confidence
modules.summary: How to challenge senior people in firms constructively, handle pushback and hold the authority's position without becoming adversarial.
objectives: Recognise when and how to challenge management's account
Use evidence-based questioning to probe weak answers
Handle resistance, deflection and seniority with professionalism
syllabus: The supervisor's role: curious, sceptical and respectful
Probing techniques: follow-up, clarification and silence
Handling pushback, emotion and appeals to seniority
Role-play: challenging a chief executive

modules.title: Presenting to Committees and Panels
modules.summary: How to prepare and deliver concise, persuasive presentations to internal committees, panels and senior decision-makers, and how to handle questions.
objectives: Prepare a clear, evidence-based paper and presentation
Present recommendations persuasively and concisely
Respond to challenging questions from senior colleagues
syllabus: Knowing the audience and the decision required
Structuring papers and slides for decision-makers
Delivery, timing and confident body language
Exercise: presenting a case to a mock committee

modules.title: Time, Workload and Case Management
modules.summary: Practical techniques for prioritising competing demands, managing a portfolio of cases and keeping work moving against deadlines.
objectives: Prioritise work by risk, urgency and impact
Plan and track multiple cases to deadline
Maintain an accurate, auditable case record
syllabus: Prioritisation frameworks and managing competing demands
Case planning, milestones and escalation
Record-keeping, document management and audit trails
Managing workload, wellbeing and knowing when to ask for help

modules.title: Working with Data
modules.summary: An introduction to using regulatory returns, firm data and spreadsheets to support supervisory work, including basic analysis, visualisation and data quality checks.
objectives: Use regulatory data and firm information to identify trends and outliers
Apply basic spreadsheet analysis and visualisation techniques
Assess data quality and recognise its limitations
syllabus: Sources of supervisory data: returns, firm data and market information
Spreadsheet essentials: sorting, filtering, pivot tables and charts
Peer comparison, trend analysis and spotting outliers
Data quality, confidentiality and secure handling

modules.title: Putting Skills into Practice: Integrated Workshop
modules.summary: Brings the programme together in a simulated supervisory exercise in which participants analyse information, meet a firm and present their findings.
objectives: Combine analysis, meeting, challenge and writing skills in a realistic scenario
Produce a clear written output from the exercise
Reflect on strengths and set personal development priorities
syllabus: Case briefing and analysis of firm information
Mock firm meeting with challenge and note-taking
Drafting a follow-up letter and short committee paper
Workshop: presentations, peer feedback and personal development plans

related.title: Investigative and Interviewing Skills for Supervisors
related.summary: An eight-module practical programme on planning and conducting supervisory interviews and turning interview evidence into sound findings.

related.title: Supervisory Judgement and Professional Practice
related.summary: A ten-module programme on forming, documenting and defending supervisory judgements, and turning them into clear findings, letters and interventions.

related.title: Assessing Board Effectiveness
related.summary: An eight-module programme showing supervisors how to assess how a board really works, from papers and decisions to culture and challenge, culminating in case-study interviews.

related.title: Core Supervisory Skills: Business Models, Governance and Risk Governance Panels
related.summary: A three-day workshop taking supervisors from business model analysis through governance interviews to a risk governance panel, using running case studies and role plays.

related.title: Foundations of Financial Regulation and Supervision
related.summary: An eight-module induction for new regulatory staff covering why we regulate, the authority's powers, risk-based supervision and a first supervisory case.

related.title: How Financial Firms Work: Business Models and Financial Statements for Supervisors
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping supervisors understand how financial firms make money, read their accounts and identify capital, liquidity and business model risks.
